title: Turn with the gyro
summary: Turn exactly 90 degrees by watching the yaw angle.

steps.title: Open the starter program
steps.text: The robot turns right 90 degrees four times, using a My Block called TurnRight.

steps.title: Why it works
steps.text: The hub has a gyro sensor that measures how far the robot has turned (the yaw angle). Turning "180 wheel degrees" can be off if a wheel slips, but turning until the gyro says 90 checks the real turn. Turning right makes the yaw go up, turning left makes it go down.

steps.title: Try it 1
steps.text: Make a TurnLeft block: spin with -20 and 20 and wait until yaw is less than the minus target.

steps.title: Try it 2
steps.text: Try a faster turn speed. Do you need to stop earlier?

steps.title: Try it 3
steps.text: Use TurnRight inside the square program instead of the steering turn.

steps.title: Take the challenge
steps.text: Start the challenge, then press ▶︎×5. The simulator checks your runs for you.
